[{"id": "qfNmWBNDvc", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udc65People Manual", "col": 12}}, {"id": "clZrizCIKn", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The People module is the heart of Churchit: it keeps every person and family your church knows, from the first-time visitor to the longtime member. Use it to keep contact details up to date, organize small groups, welcome and follow up visitors, care for people in need, and print the church directory.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "j1DtIi-ZZG", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Church Office users (the Church People Editor role) add and change people, families and groups. Church Care Team users look after care requests, visits, background checks and notes. Other staff can look people up. Members see and correct their own household in the member portal.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "_R-t8aLCeS", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The People workspace starts with the work that waits for you: Open Care Requests and the Care Board (for the care team and managers), Follow-ups Needed, Pending Join Requests, New Connection Cards and Open Possible Duplicates. Shortcuts open the Rolodex, the Check-In Station and the Map of Addresses.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "wGOS7gOW1F", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Under them, cards count the members, families and groups, the first-time visitors, the new members of the last 30 days and the people who may have stopped coming. The charts show new members by month and baptisms by year.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "gF2VhtoFOg", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The People sidebar has the pages you use every day at the top: People, Families, Groups, Rolodex and Church Directory. The other pages are in folders: Care, Visitors & Follow-up, Group Tools, Membership, Dates, Letters, Data and Setup. Each folder ends with its reports.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "9FEqZkWWi9", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udc64Person", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fnqG5ZwuIX", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Person is one record for each human being your church knows: members, regular attenders, visitors, children, and contacts such as a missionary's supporter. Everything else in Churchit links to the person: their family, their groups, their attendance, their giving and the care they received.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "UfPPEpFQsz", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "", "col": 12}}, {"id": "VtTmyXU6P2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example
Maria visits for the first time and fills in a Connection Card. Churchit adds her as a Person with the Membership Visitor. Over the next months she joins a small group, and the office adds her baptism as a life event. When she joins the church, the office adds a Membership life event, and her Membership changes to Member.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "DiiKx4hHCL", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Add a person", "col": 12}}, {"id": "0Fzu6aghVs", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Open People and click Add Person.
2. Type the First Name and Last Name. While you type, Churchit warns you if a person with the same name and email or phone may already exist.
3. Choose the Membership and pick the Family if the person belongs to one.
4. Add their email, phone and address in the Contact section, and the Birth life event in Life Events.
5. Save.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "kL7G81rCnZ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The form has three tabs, and a Church Fields tab when your church adds its own fields:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "9I1mGPR-qi", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Details: the name, membership and household at the top, then Other Names, Health and Emergency, Contact, Life Events and Relationships.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "qcgnyt1lAN", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Records: the envelope number, how the person was added, Roles and Gifts (positions and skills), Directory and Portal (the photo, the directory choices and the portal login) and Letters to the Church.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "z2TXRKcMfA", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Connections: the person's records in groups: Involvement, Care, Giving, Membership and Follow-up, and figures such as Last Attended and Times Served. Each group shows only to the roles that can read it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "cSpC2qcMcy", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Click the (i) next to a label to read the help for that field, or click ..., then Take the Tour, for a short tour of the form. The People list opens on Active people. Clear the Status filter at the top to see everyone.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "b-fsS_EOjj", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Membership and Status", "col": 12}}, {"id": "yIUV4GlOLl", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "These two fields say how the person is connected to the church:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "zpE_p8Y_dR", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Membership: Member, Regular Attender, Visitor or Contact. When you add a Membership life event, Membership changes to Member. You can add more membership types.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "DYeREHcwov", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Status: Active for everyone who still takes part. When someone leaves, set it to Inactive and pick the Inactive Reason, such as Moved away. Inactive Since shows the day the status changed, and is cleared when the person becomes Active again.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "qrfLlPkYYr", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Reports, the Church Directory, the Members card and the bulletin count a person as a member only when Membership is Member and Status is Active. The Visitor Log shows new people whose Membership is Visitor or empty. The New Members (30 days) card counts the active members whose first Membership life event is in the last 30 days.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Q1LcdjYA_M", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Two Inactive Reasons are set for you and cannot be deleted or renamed: Deceased (when you add a Death life event) and Transferred to another church (when you confirm a member transfer out). Add your own on the Inactive Reason list.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "8BV8PYdZWZ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Source shows how the person was first added: Desk, Import, Check-In, Connection Card, Portal, Sign-Up or Form. It never changes.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "mNQEeQqgpU", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Life events, birthdays and ages", "col": 12}}, {"id": "g-WqtmSSp3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Record birth, baptism, membership, marriage and death in the Life Events table.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bCBZRcQGvP", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- The Birth event fills in Birth Date and Age, so you do not type them. When you know only the month and day of a birthday, enter any year and tick No Year: the birthday still counts, but Birth Date and Age stay blank.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "A-agqDHBQh", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- A Death event ticks Deceased, fills in Deceased Date, sets the Status to Inactive and, if no Inactive Reason is set, the reason to Deceased. The person's spouse becomes Widowed. People who have died are left out of the birthday and anniversary lists and cards, the bulletin, the Church Directory, the Rolodex, the Check-In Station and Church Emails.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "eD32lFQIOs", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- A date cannot be in the future, and a death or anniversary cannot be before the birth. A person has one Birth and one Death event.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "kAXU5HBy37", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- When you add a person who has died to a function's attendance after the date of death, or to a group, a sign-up or a pledge, Churchit saves it with an orange warning. History is often entered late.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "MqG6I7PxC3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Life Stage is Adult or Child. It comes from the person's household role in their family, or else from their age: a person is an Adult from the Adult Age in People Settings (18 at first). Ages and life stages update every night.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "eAODb9qFf4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Birthdays This Week and Birthdays This Month (in the Dates folder) list each birthday on its date this year, with the age that the person turns. A February 29 birthday is listed on February 28 in other years. A week starts on the first day of the week in System Settings (Sunday on a new site).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "9NpI0MIIty", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Names", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Aa29d9Xqz5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Middle Name sits between the first and last names, and Nickname under the last name.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "kGgtWURvTa", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Click Other Names to add a Prefix (Mr., Mrs., Dr., Rev.), a Suffix (Jr., Sr., III) and a Previous Last Name, such as a maiden name. A search for a person also finds the nickname and the previous last name.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ydh-XbdtzA", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Display Name is filled in for you: the nickname (or the first name), the last name and the suffix, such as Bob Smith Jr.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "yXDDrrKjgR", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- You cannot change a person's ID. To correct a name, change the First Name or Last Name. To join two records of one person, merge them (see below).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "tPyQEgbS3j", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Emails, phones and addresses", "col": 12}}, {"id": "t2sEv1FdiC", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A person can have several emails, phone numbers and addresses, each in its own table.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "S2_b2Fee0D", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Primary: the first row is the primary one, and only one row in each table can be primary. Church Emails, the directory, the Rolodex, greetings and portal invitations use the primary email and phone. Ticking a new primary row unticks the old one.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "WsnQearyNS", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Texts on a phone number: untick it on a number that cannot get texts, such as a landline. A new number takes it from its Phone Type: each Phone Type has New Numbers Receive Texts, which is ticked for every type except Home. Changing a number's type sets it again from the new type.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "os7i1V4O90", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Mailing: tick it on the address that gets mail from the church. Returned shows that mail sent there came back.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "mlM7hojYhx", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Bounced on an email shows that email to this address came back. Church Emails skip it, and the form shows an orange line when the primary email has bounced (see the Communications manual). Churchit clears it when you change the address.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "aQU_kkORuJ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- An email or phone number can be on one person only, so the same person is not entered twice. Churchit matches phone numbers however they are written: (202) 555-0147 and 202.555.0147 are the same.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ecqzm3-5nx", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Shared emails and phones. When two people really use the same email or phone, such as a couple's shared email or a child using a parent's phone, enter it on both. Leave Shared From blank on the row of the owner, usually the person who uses it to sign in to the member portal. On everyone else's row, set Shared From to the owner. A family may use a member's email or phone without Shared From.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "rVga_kPycO", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example
John and Mary Smith share the email smiths@example.com. John signs in to the member portal with it, so on John's row Shared From is blank. On Mary's row, Shared From is John. A Church Email to both of them goes to the address once.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "O9f7GwOuLq", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Marriage and family", "col": 12}}, {"id": "hJk7c6yekS", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The third column at the top of the Details tab shows the person's family and marriage.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "OxWOJFC03n", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Marital Status is Single, Married, Widowed or Divorced. Spouse and Anniversary show only for Married and Widowed people.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "nd_Dne6rcw", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- When you give a Married person a spouse, the spouse is linked back as Married and shares the anniversary. The couple shares one family: if only one has a family, the other joins it. If neither has one, Churchit makes a family named after the person you save.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "icTSNypONn", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- When you set a person to Divorced or Single, the marriage ends for both people: the spouse and the anniversary are removed from both.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "VM7HmChocB", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- A Widowed person keeps the spouse and the anniversary.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "U_PxSG0q0G", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- When a married person moves to another family, their spouse moves too if they were in the same family.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "s3OBv9_Ogs", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- No Year under the anniversary works as for birthdays.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "LEJUwb-N2I", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "New Family From Person. Click Actions, then New Family From Person, to make a family for a person who has a last name and is not yet the primary contact of a family, such as a married son who starts his own household. The person becomes its primary contact. If a family with that name already exists in your church, the person joins it instead.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "0V-6IoRVRx", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Health and emergency", "col": 12}}, {"id": "4nRBGJmmKp", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Medical Notes is for health information that the church needs to know, such as a condition or a medicine. Only Church Manager, Church People Editor and Church Check-In users can see it, and only Church Managers and Church People Editors can change it. It is never printed, and members do not see it in the member portal. The Check-In Station shows it to check-in volunteers.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "qVbEB8II4x", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Emergency Contact Name and Emergency Contact Phone are for someone with no household adult in Churchit, such as a visiting child. The same users see them.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "mtO9j995Z5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Allergies: the member can change it in the member portal. The Check-In Station shows it, and name tags can print it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "rLXecwhlBx", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Changes to fields that only some users can see do not show in the timeline of the person.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "IcgtCZDbvE", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Roles in the church", "col": 12}}, {"id": "QOYCoA1Vuh", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Add the person's roles, such as Elder or Sunday School Teacher, in the Positions table on the Records tab, with a start and end date. You can add more position types.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "z0zKhWV7CG", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- On a position type, Assign to Person adds the position to a person.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "32ZVHzl2ux", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Tick Is Single-Person Role for a role that one person holds at a time, such as Pastor. Churchit then refuses to give it to a second person of the same church while someone holds it with no End Date.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "lZ1l20xLBN", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- The End Date of a position cannot be before its Start Date.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "uAfMgPDHvK", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- The Person Positions Ending This Month report shows the positions that end in the next 60 days.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "UoKyk54mt4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Photo and the directory", "col": 12}}, {"id": "2N7ssEfsxL", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Add a photo on the Records tab. It shows in the Church Directory, the member portal's directory, group lists, the Rolodex and the Check-In Station.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ThqFN_nbHM", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "In the Directory and Portal section:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "HwTK-GY4Zn", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Show Email in the Member Directory, and the same boxes for Phone, Address and Birthday, decide what other members see in the member portal's directory. New people start with the choices in People Settings (New People Show Their Email and the others): email, phone and birthday shown, address hidden. People added from a card or a first portal sign-in share nothing until they choose. Members change these choices themselves in the member portal.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "IBQ3E3TT6b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Hide from Directory and Bulletin leaves the person out of the printed Church Directory, the member directory, and the birthdays and anniversaries of the bulletin.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "BVysZYAQxl", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Keep Out of Churchit's AI Features keeps the person away from AI (see the Foundations manual).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "xBRoZgi2Jm", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Other records on the person", "col": 12}}, {"id": "M19XglH2Zl", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Letters to the Church (Records tab): letters from this person (see Letters in the Communications manual).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "M9u3NvkFPG", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Activity at the bottom of the form: who opened the record, the person's notes, visits, care requests, member transfers, connection cards and life events, each on its day. Each kind shows its 20 newest records, and a life event shows only when its full date is known. You see only what your role and your church let you open.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "PD3RmCQHp8", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Alert notes show in red at the top of the form (see Person Notes).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "IaSmJo8vMa", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- The form also shows a line with the person's latest background check, and Unsubscribed from Church Emails when they stopped all Church Emails.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "vkrO6j6D0u", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "School grade", "col": 12}}, {"id": "845Kb5mNI-", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Type the year that a child finishes high school in Graduation Year. Churchit shows the school grade in Grade and updates it each day: Kindergarten in the school year that starts 13 years before graduation, then Grade 1 to Grade 12, then Graduated. The grade goes up on the first day of the month in School Year Starts In in People Settings (August at first). The Graduation Year field shows for children, and for adults who have one.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "klpoF9oboM", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example
With the school year starting in August, a child with Graduation Year 2030 is in Grade 8 on July 31, 2026 and in Grade 9 on August 1, 2026.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "2LGgwitEHi", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Envelope numbers", "col": 12}}, {"id": "1TAnaXn7oS", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Envelope Number is the number on a person's offering envelopes, or the reference on their bank gifts. Two people in one church cannot have the same number. Type it in any Person field, such as a donation row, to find the person. A signed-in member sees it on the Give page as the reference to use.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "FL7FwDQ9oN", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Member QR Card", "col": 12}}, {"id": "vjQhxyYHYI", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Member QR Card print format prints a wallet card, the size of a bank card, with the church name, the person's name, photo and a QR code. Open the person, click the print icon and choose Member QR Card. At the Check-In Station, the person shows the card to the camera with Scan Card to check in quickly.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "66OFaG7rRy", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Skills, interests and spiritual gifts", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Zgj87hO2RI", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Use Skills, Interests and Gifts on the Records tab to record what the person can do, what they like to do and their spiritual gifts. Each Skill has a category: Skill, Interest or Spiritual Gift. Churchit starts with twelve spiritual gifts from Romans 12, 1 Corinthians 12, Ephesians 4 and 1 Peter 4. Church Managers and Church People Editors can add more.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "1tmr5m2ajU", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example
You need people who can play the piano. Open the People list in Report view, add a filter on Skill (Person Skill) equals Piano, and save the report. You can then email the list or keep it as a smart list (see Lists of People).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "EGLV6svBlY", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Relationships to other households", "col": 12}}, {"id": "eSYvPNeoJ_", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Use the Relationships table to record a relative who lives in another household, for example a grandparent. Record the relationship on one person only: the other person sees it on their Connections tab. Use the Family's Members table for people in the same household: you cannot choose the person themselves or someone in the same family.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "k9acQ_R7-F", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Church fields", "col": 12}}, {"id": "0i0063l6yP", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A System Manager can add the church's own fields to the Person and Family forms, for example a T-shirt size:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "LNBOGOHPWC", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Open Customize Form and choose Person or Family.
2. Find the row Church Fields at the end of the fields table, and add the new field below it. Do not tick Mandatory: Churchit adds people from cards, imports and the member portal without church fields.
3. To show a Person field only to Church Managers, Church People Editors and check-in users, set its Perm Level to 1. Do not set a Perm Level on a Family field: nobody could see it.
4. Click Update.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "j0LiE8ygDf", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The field shows on the Church Fields tab, and you can filter lists on it. When a later update moves fields on the form, open Customize Form, choose Person or Family and click Actions, then Reset Layout. Your fields stay. Never use Reset All Customizations, which deletes them.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "hDImCGrAQY", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Birthday and anniversary emails", "col": 12}}, {"id": "YzgZinHYiK", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Churchit can email a greeting to each person on their birthday, and to each married couple on their anniversary. A System Manager turns on a copy of the Birthday Greeting or Anniversary Greeting notification (see Notifications in the Communications manual) and can change its words.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "IyJX0aG2sf", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- The birthday greeting goes to the primary email of each active person whose birthday is today, also with No Year.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AbIP-D6_MC", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- The anniversary greeting goes to the primary contact of the family when that person is married, and names both spouses. A Widowed person gets none.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bV4j_S5TiW", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- People who have died get no greeting. Hide from Directory and Bulletin does not stop the greetings.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "p7eqIbzKfr", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- To send a greeting some days early, type the number of days in Days Before or After on the copy.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "_iuHcjpUli", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Merge two records of one person", "col": 12}}, {"id": "lvgzIZX3z8", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When one person has two records, merge them. Open the record that you do not want to keep, click ..., then Merge Into..., choose the person to keep and click Merge. Only users who can delete people, such as a Church Manager, can merge.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "IjLNjmXhMW", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Merging two people
You cannot undo a merge. The removed record is deleted for good.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "1G5mwO9L5P", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When both people have a different value for a detail, the merge window shows a table: choose the value to keep in each row. The rest moves by itself:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "o7-fX5lmKL", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Everything that names the removed record moves to the kept one: attendance, giving, groups, ministry teams, care, prayers, comments, attachments and history.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bbM-ddpEzs", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Emails, phones, addresses, life events, positions, letters, skills and relationships are added to the kept record, without repeats. The kept record's primary email, phone and address stay primary.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "cMPMUJVEPn", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- The portal login moves to the kept record when it has none. The kept person stays in their own family, or joins the family of the removed record when they have none.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "PUnRMlSh6k", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- A Possible Duplicate for the two is marked Merged.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "YxQixL7MAr", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Churchit refuses to merge two people who both have a portal login, who have different spouses, who are married to each other, or who belong to different churches. A Portal User or an Envelope Number that the other person still has cannot move: clear it on that person first. When both records came from an import, merge them in the old system too, or the next import adds the record again.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "nswAQrIVs_", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Remove the personal data of a person", "col": 12}}, {"id": "XnMJxLZ-VJ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When a person asks the church to forget them, a Church Manager or a System Manager opens the person and clicks ..., then Remove Personal Data. The record stays, with the first name Anonymized and the last name, so that their giving and attendance still count in reports.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "5RCC-nJuQx", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Removing personal data
You cannot undo Remove Personal Data.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "-kqf94OSs4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Churchit removes the names except the last name, the emails, phones, addresses, letters, photo, medical notes, emergency contact, allergies, anniversary, skills, church fields, portal login and Imported ID. The person is hidden from the directory, and the portal login is disabled.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "RxEseH9UDq", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- The Birth life event is removed. Other life events keep their type and date, so the yearly counts stay right.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "PBr2E3yVYo", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- The person leaves their family and their spouse, and loses their relationships. A family with no members left is anonymized too.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "CWmf41ueLI", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Records about the person lose their history, comments and attachments: background checks, care requests, counseling cases, giving statements, serving assignments and others. Their Person Notes, Connection Cards, Form Responses, group join requests and the Pickup Restrictions that protect them are deleted. Their open follow-up cards are closed. Their answers and typed details on function sign-ups are removed, also on guest sign-ups made with one of their email addresses. Their Gender becomes Unknown, and the family name loses their first name.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "LjkO5l301w", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Emails and texts sent to the person lose their address and text. Other records that name the person keep the link but lose the person's name and email.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "JjxmiltpUi", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- AI chats and suggestions about the person and their requests are deleted (see the Foundations manual).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "tHUTHqH20c", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When a System Manager approves a member's Personal Data Deletion Request, Churchit removes the data in the same way.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "USB9heto9G", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "On a schedule. In People Settings, set Remove Personal Data After (Years Inactive). Each day, Churchit then removes the personal data of up to 50 people who have been Inactive that long, the earliest first, and adds a comment with the reason. People who have died are kept. 0 (the default) never removes data. The Personal Data Due for Removal report (in the Data folder) shows who is next and when. To keep a person's data, set their Status back to Active before that date.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ZrP-zg1fAJ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Deleting a person
Deleting a person is different: it removes the person from their family and spouse, removes the relationships that others have with them, and deletes their membership history, so they drop out of the Membership Changes report. Use Remove Personal Data when someone asks to be forgotten, and Merge for a duplicate.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bwJnZQkzRr", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Person Notes", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ihmrz6W8H_", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Person Notes keep what staff know about a person: a phone call, a visit, or something to remember. To add one, open the person, click Actions, then Add Person Note. Pick a Category, write the note and save. The Date is today unless you change it. For a call or a visit, pick how you were in touch in Contact.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "1_j7Y7zJfu", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- A person's notes show in the Activity list at the bottom of their form, on the day each note records. Tick Pinned to keep a note at the top.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "YAICihYJRn", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Tick Alert to show the note in red at the top of the person's form, for example \"Hard of hearing. Face him when you speak.\"", "col": 12}}, {"id": "GJ4HaFComZ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- You see only the notes that your role may read. Notes cannot be shared with other users, and Churchit keeps no change history of them.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "5fy6WBooz7", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Note categories. A Note Category decides who reads and adds its notes. Churchit starts with three: every staff member reads General, and only the care team and Church Managers read Pastoral Care and Benevolence (the case notes of alms requests). A Church Manager can add categories:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "KUMZc8HJ5J", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Roles That Read Notes: the roles that can read the notes. Blank lets all staff read them.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Aa12262FMe", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Roles That Add Notes: the roles that can add and change the notes. Blank lets all staff add them. A role that can add but not read cannot open a note again after saving it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "2bwVunkLnt", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Private: only the person who wrote a note can read it, not even a Church Manager.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fVYqZjUBEh", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "With more than one church, every church uses the same categories, and only a Church Manager of the main church can change their roles.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "WktQSECQfn", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example
The pastor visits Mr. Jones in hospital and adds a Pastoral Care note: \"Surgery went well, home on Friday. Wife Ruth asked for meals.\" The church secretary, who is not on the care team, does not see the note.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ne14JrEcnI", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Draft a Note With AI. When AI is turned on (see the Foundations manual), open a person, click Actions, then Draft Note With AI. Choose Person Note or Visitation Log, paste or type what you remember, and click Draft. Click Open the Draft: the form opens filled in and not saved. Check each field and save. Notes and visits are private records, so this needs an AI model that keeps no copy of your data. Do not share the AI chat that holds your notes.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "RyIBLlXvxR", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udd11Logins", "col": 12}}, {"id": "YlnRUO383I", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Members and staff sign in with a login (a user). A member's login opens the member portal, where they see their own household. A staff login opens the desk, where they do their work.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "SkZ_y47jd_", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Invite a member to the member portal", "col": 12}}, {"id": "PmFlnR1H3H", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Make sure that the person has a primary email address.
2. Open the person and click Actions, then Invite to Portal.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "1Dm01seUmd", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Churchit makes a login with the Church User role, links it to the person, and emails them an invitation. If a login with that email already exists, Churchit links it instead, unless another person already has that login or it belongs to a church you cannot see. The button shows only to users who can change the person, and only while the person has an email and no login. It needs an outgoing email account.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "U91_R3vape", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Churchit also links a login to a person by itself at the first sign-in, when one person has the same primary email and no login (see Portal accounts under Member Portal).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "f13yaddCK0", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A visitor who is not signed in sees on the portal: \"Part of the church but no login yet? Ask the church office to invite you.\"", "col": 12}}, {"id": "X1Dlym2ueX", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Staff logins", "col": 12}}, {"id": "81CSbe6142", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Staff and volunteers who work in the desk need a user with a Role Profile that fits their job:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "oth1zSDhM4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "
Role ProfileWhat it gives

", "col": 12}}, {"id": "_g834WEbFj", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To give someone several jobs, add more than one Role Profile to their user. After they sign in, each person opens the page for their work: a check-in volunteer opens the Check-In Station, a follow-up volunteer opens Follow-up Cards, and other staff open Summary. Linking a staff login to a Person does not change which churches the staff member sees (see the Foundations manual).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "j58Eput9Nj", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Two-factor authentication", "col": 12}}, {"id": "yRbOgltiTQ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Two-factor authentication asks for a code as well as the password at login, so a stolen password alone does not open the church's records. We recommend it for every staff login, because staff can see personal and medical details.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "4Lmzpfka8J", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Open System Settings and go to the Login tab.
2. Under Two Factor Authentication, tick Enable Two Factor Auth.
3. Choose the method: OTP App (a code from an app such as Google Authenticator), SMS (set up SMS Settings first) or Email.
4. Save. Each user sets it up the next time they log in.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "YEL3C9QC_k", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "This asks everyone for a code, members too. To ask only staff, open the All role and untick Two Factor Authentication, then tick it on the Church Staff, Church Manager, Church Check-In and Church Follow-up roles.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "VjmaVm916D", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Single sign-on", "col": 12}}, {"id": "BWFzNJsLS_", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "With single sign-on, people use one account for Churchit and other apps. A System Manager sets it up.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ZkkFqywisP", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Sign in to Churchit with another account, such as Google, Keycloak or Authentik:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "1lAg3zGSjd", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Open Social Login Key and choose the Social Login Provider: Google, Keycloak, or Custom for Authentik and other OpenID Connect providers.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "iCMgGRTUPn", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "2. Type the Client ID and Client Secret that the other system gives you. For Keycloak, type the realm's address in Base URL. For Custom, type a one-word Provider Name, such as authentik, the Authorize URL, Access Token URL and API Endpoint, and set Redirect URL to /api/method/frappe.integrations.oauth2_logins.custom/authentik.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "O3kd1o8VqJ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "3. Set Sign ups to Deny, so only people who already have a login can sign in. Churchit finds the login by the email address.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "HXtWU93kfx", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "4. Tick Enable Social Login and save. In the other system, set the redirect address to your site address followed by the Redirect URL.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "wWKo0Q-3_e", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Use Churchit logins in another app, such as a wiki or Nextcloud:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "hL1-UeB1qT", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Open OAuth Client and type the App Name.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "7oXHFAAhxF", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "2. Set Scopes to openid, and type the app's redirect address in Redirect URIs and Default Redirect URI.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "lqvQ4tuqGv", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "3. In Allowed Roles, add the roles that can use the app, for example Church Staff, Church Manager, Church Check-In and Church Follow-up for all staff. If you leave it empty, every desk login can use the app.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "VVmVwU41pO", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "4. Set Token Endpoint Auth Method to Client Secret Post and save.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fkSFuFXGlV", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "5. In the app, type the Client ID, the Client Secret and the address: your site address followed by /.well-known/openid-configuration.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "B9LybBexVD", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "If no other app needs to add itself, untick Enable Dynamic Client Registration in OAuth Settings.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Z62oZd1svz", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udc68\u200d\ud83d\udc69\u200d\ud83d\udc67\u200d\ud83d\udc66Family", "col": 12}}, {"id": "XRXLfMLD4W", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Family is one household: the people who live together, such as parents and their children. The family holds the household's address, its photo, the role of each person in it, and who may collect its children after check-in. A person can be in one household only.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "PUpifssx6Z", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "", "col": 12}}, {"id": "LeZNdRJbFD", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example
The Smith family has John (the primary contact), his wife Mary, their two children, and John's mother Ruth, who lives with them. John and Mary are Adults, the children are Children, and Ruth is an Other Adult: she lives there but is not a parent. Mary's sister Anne may collect the children on Sundays, so she is an Authorized Pickup.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "lXGperW0h-", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "See the diagram in the online manual", "col": 12}}, {"id": "duoI0sRNn7", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Add a family", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fJb4atZL6v", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Open Families and click Add Family.
2. Add the people in Family Members, with each one's Relationship to Primary Contact, such as Wife or Son. You can also pick the Family on each Person form.
3. Set the Primary Contact, the person the family is named after, such as Smith - John.
4. Add the Home Address, and tick Mailing on the address that gets mail. Shared phone numbers and emails go in Household Phone and Email.
5. Save.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fVefrFNYuY", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Good to know", "col": 12}}, {"id": "2e-iFIh8oo", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- To move a person from another household, remove them from that family first, or change Family on their Person form.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "XNcrS7rsjZ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- The primary contact and their spouse are labelled Husband and Wife from the Spouse field of the Person. A member's spouse with no relationship gets one from the member, such as Daughter-in-law for a son's wife.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "mcQ7JXwd6g", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- When you change the Primary Contact, the family is renamed, and each relationship changes to the relationship to the new primary contact. A relationship that Churchit cannot work out is cleared, and a message names the members to set by hand.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "QlcugsvInq", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- With more than one church, a family belongs to the church of its Primary Contact.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "KEDTgr7zpe", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Household roles", "col": 12}}, {"id": "a33D_C1IjQ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Each member of a family has a Household Role:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "LjlScnQKcw", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Adult: a responsible adult of the household, such as a parent. Adults may edit the household in the member portal and always collect its children.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "0cvk5ArXfn", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Other Adult: an adult who lives there but has no authority over the children, such as a grandparent, a grown son or a lodger.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "QExSQrrQkF", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Child: a dependent.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "GZsQY9fF-X", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When you save a family with a Primary Contact, Churchit fills in each blank role:
- The primary contact and their spouse are Adults.
- A son, daughter, stepchild or grandchild under the Adult Age is a Child.
- Any other member at or above the Adult Age is an Other Adult.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "9uPWVkYMzQ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "If Churchit cannot tell, for example for a nephew under 18 or a member with no birth date, it leaves the role blank: set it by hand. Churchit never changes a role that someone set. If you link a spouse after the family has a Primary Contact, check the spouse's role: Churchit may have set Other Adult, so set Adult by hand. The role also sets the person's Life Stage.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "I2iF3UtCA5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A letter or mailing label can address a family by its Adults, for example \"John & Jane Smith\", or \"John Smith & Jane Doe\" when their last names differ. A nickname replaces the first name, people who have died are left out, and a family with no Adult is addressed by its family name. When the primary contact leaves the family, the family has no primary contact until you set a new one. In a print format, write {{ salutation(doc.family) }}.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "KFLDG6m2m0", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Merge two families", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Z3dlzgz4tW", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When one household has two Family records, open the one that you do not want to keep, click ..., then Merge Into..., choose the family to keep and click Merge. The members, emails, phones, addresses and Authorized Pickups move to the kept family, without repeats. The kept family keeps its name and Primary Contact.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "M8WNc0quPo", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A kept family with no Primary Contact takes the one of the removed family, and each Household Role stays. A member who came from a family with another primary contact loses their relationship: set it again. Only users who can delete families can merge them. You cannot undo a merge.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "hL2SEd9438", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Authorized Pickups", "col": 12}}, {"id": "-X7W2ytgdW", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Adults of a household may always collect its children after check-in. To let another person collect them, such as a grandparent, an aunt or a neighbor, open the family and click + next to Authorized Pickup in Connections (or open Authorized Pickups in the Care folder). Set the Person, the Relationship and any Notes, such as \"Sundays only\". The person must have a Person record. An Other Adult of the household can be one.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "gzzay8gH67", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Adults already collect, so only an Other Adult or someone outside the household can be added, once for each family. Deleting a family deletes its Authorized Pickups. Verify Pickup at the Check-In Station shows these people with their photos (see the Ministries manual). Only Church Manager and Church People Editor users of the family's church can open Authorized Pickups. Do not write custody details in the notes: use a Pickup Restriction.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "hHhQspT1Nd", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Pickup Restrictions", "col": 12}}, {"id": "-mJISHzX2z", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Pickup Restriction names someone who may not collect a child, for example because of a court order. It applies also to an Adult of the child's household.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "kwVq7QmZp_", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Pick the Child.
2. Pick the Restricted Person, or type their name in Restricted Name when they have no Person record.
3. In What the Volunteer Sees, write what the check-in volunteer must know, such as how to recognize the person and whom to call.
4. Set Valid Until to the last day, or leave it empty.
5. Write the Reason and attach the Court Order as a private file.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "hQFi-vlgAG", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Only Church Manager and Church People Editor users can open a Pickup Restriction. At Verify Pickup, the station shows the restricted person, the child, What the Volunteer Sees and the last day, but never the reason or the court order. It refuses to release the child to that person, and only a Church Manager can override it, with a reason that Churchit records. A page to the parents does not go to the restricted person. The list shows Active or Ended for each restriction.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "EL9oSl8DuI", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example
A court order says that a child's father may not collect her. The office adds a Pickup Restriction with the father as Restricted Person and \"Call Pastor Tom at once\" in What the Volunteer Sees. If the father comes with the pickup tag, the station shows the warning in red and does not let the volunteer release the child.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ryfhAvA47_", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83c\udfe0Member Portal", "col": 12}}, {"id": "qcYRQ_3jRV", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The member portal is the app where members see and correct their own records (see Member Portal in the Website manual for a tour of all its pages). This section explains the parts that staff manage: logins, households and the member directory.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "HI35frvi_C", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Portal accounts", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Do86w55MGJ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A member needs a login to use the member portal. There are two ways:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "trRhw4Ryup", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Invite: staff click Actions, then Invite to Portal, on the Person (see Logins).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fhxs8WOwjk", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- First sign-in: when your church lets people sign up on the website, or a System Manager adds a Website User, Churchit connects the new login to a Person at its first sign-in. It looks in the church of the login for one living person with the same primary email (not a Shared From row) and no login.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "SOejGpTXg1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "If it finds no one, it adds a Visitor with the Source Portal, who shares nothing in the directory. If it finds more than one, it connects nobody and lists them under Possible Duplicates: merge them, or set the Portal User on the right person. Staff logins are never connected this way.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "BTr5LiONM-", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "My Household", "col": 12}}, {"id": "RFIOFPC1M_", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Members see their household on the My Household page of the member portal: the Family photo and name, the mailing address and the living members with their Household Role, and the age of each Child.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "_hdKhUWkHc", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- A member clicks Edit beside their own name to change their details. An Adult can also edit each Child under the Adult Age.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "5jL3NOmm-p", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- An Adult can click Change photo to put a new photo on the family. The photo is public, so other members see it in the directory.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "rlgaEgu4L0", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- An Adult can click Add a child (younger than the Adult Age), and type the first name, last name, birthday and gender. The child joins the household with the role Child and the relationship Son or Daughter, as a Visitor with the Source Portal. If the child may already be in Churchit, a Possible Duplicate opens for staff to check.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "InWUegsust", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Members cannot add another adult or remove anyone. The page tells them to contact the church office.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ORGtgOarXx", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "My Details", "col": 12}}, {"id": "VtR5UbPEME", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "On My Details, a member changes their name, gender, birthday, allergies, emails, phone numbers (with the primary ones), marital status, anniversary and photo. The birthday goes into the Birth life event, so Birth Date and Age follow. Members cannot change their addresses there: they tell the church office.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "wkUd18pUvy", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Hide me from the member directory leaves them out of the member directory, the printed Church Directory and the bulletin's birthdays and anniversaries.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "_yg6KccaWC", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- They choose whether the directory shows their email, phone, address and birthday.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Wi24ZgMRYz", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Leave me out of the church's AI features keeps them away from Churchit's AI features. The part says whether the church uses AI now, so a member can choose before AI is turned on. A parent can tick it for a child. Only the person, a parent of a child, or a System Manager can clear it again.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "R4MZWu2slJ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Send Details Link", "col": 12}}, {"id": "5VIOqzQumF", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To let a person correct their details without a login, open the Person and click Actions, then Send Details Link. Churchit emails a link to an Update Your Details page, where the person can change their name, gender, birthday, allergies, emails, phones, marital status, anniversary and directory choices. They cannot change addresses.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "VScBgtrq-Q", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The link works once, for 7 days. To send a new link, click Send Details Link again. The item shows only when you can change the person and they have a primary email. The person's timeline shows when you sent it. The site must have an outgoing email account.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "6AxUZNl1ZC", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example
Before printing the new directory, the office sends a details link to every family without a login. Each family checks its phone numbers and birthdays and clicks Save. The office does not retype anything.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ENvkTKD5Y3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Member directory", "col": 12}}, {"id": "BTU4weUEfd", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Directory page of the member portal lists the people of the member's church, so members can find each other. To turn it on, tick Member Directory in People Settings.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "q8zMGq4oB6", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- It lists people whose Status is Active and whose Membership is filled in and is not Visitor or Contact, such as Members and Regular Attenders. It leaves out people who have died and people who hide from the directory.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "32zjprySc0", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- The same people can open it, also when they hide themselves from it. Others see a note to contact the church office.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "qrWKkiQU-m", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Each family is one entry, with its photo and names. The primary email, primary phone, mailing address and birthday (day and month only) show only when the person chose to share them.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "dfZxxo3ljz", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Save contact adds an entry to the phone's contacts, with only what the entry shows.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "11dHjLCFXL", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Only public photos show. When you attach a photo in the desk, clear Private if members may see it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "lMPypd5Hko", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udc65Group", "col": 12}}, {"id": "wfBlSFxnUR", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Group is a set of people with a shared purpose: a small group, a Sunday School class, a choir, a committee. Groups have members with roles such as Leader, meet at regular times, and can let members join from the member portal or the website.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "gepNgJb6p-", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "", "col": 12}}, {"id": "y31EdTQ2mQ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example
The Tuesday Night Bible Study is a public small group of up to 12 people, led by Tom and Sarah. A visitor finds it on the website's Find a Group page and clicks Ask to Join. Tom gets an email and accepts the request on Lead a Group in the member portal. The day after each meeting, Tom gets a reminder if nobody has recorded who came.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "G5t_uyfZqj", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Add a group", "col": 12}}, {"id": "z8K-NeBnJV", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Open Groups and click Add Group.
2. Type the Name (two groups of one church cannot share a name) and choose the Group Type. The type fills in its defaults on the Joining tab.
3. Add the people in Members, each with a Group Role, such as Leader or Member.
4. On the Joining tab, choose who can see and join the group (see below).
5. Save.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "F8vXI_Kpd7", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To give the group a regular meeting time, click Actions, then Set Up Meetings (see Group meetings in the Ministries manual). Meets then shows when and where the group meets, such as Weekly on Tuesday at 7:00 PM. The Connections tab shows the group's ministry, meetings, join requests and files. To email the group, use Email Group or Email Selected under the Members table, or Actions, then Send Church Email.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "O7oZ-m5OYg", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Group types and roles", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ZBkx0BWBLw", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Group Type is a kind of group, such as Small Group, Class or Youth Group. Its defaults for Public, Show in Portal, Requires Approval and Capacity fill in when you choose the type on a group. A later change to a type does not change existing groups. Every church uses the same types.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "gmBKfbxM-e", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A person leads a group when their Group Role has Leads the Group ticked. Churchit ticks it on the Leader role. Tick it on other roles whose people lead, such as Teacher or Host. Leaders record attendance, message the group and decide join requests.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "tw1H4-2SHs", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Joining a group", "col": 12}}, {"id": "uu9degsMck", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "On the Joining tab:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "CFJMjqxuxr", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Public and Show in Portal: members can join an active group that has both, on the Groups page of the member portal or the website's Find a Group page.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "igBX5Y8RQD", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Show in Directory: lists the group's members in the printed Church Directory, when its Group List and Group Members options are ticked.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "I0kMHTscWc", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Capacity: the most members that members can add by joining. 0 means no limit. Staff can still add more in the desk. A leader cannot approve a join request while the group is full: raise Capacity or decline.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "jNMLuYhsyw", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Close Enrollment On: after this date, nobody can join or ask to join.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "eGnuM5e536", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Requires Approval: a member who clicks Join sends a Group Join Request, and each leader gets an email. A leader clicks Approve or Decline on Lead a Group, or staff open the request. Approval adds the person as a Member. The person gets an email with the answer.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "1H7I3WAMJW", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A member leaves a group with Leave this group in the member portal. The only leader of a group cannot leave: name another leader first.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "MSUs_M4sIq", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "In the member portal, a member who opens one of their groups sees who else is in it, with each person's photo if it is public. An email or phone shows only when that person shares it in the member directory, and only while the Member Directory is on. A person who hides from the directory shows no photo, email or phone there. Leaders see the contact details that people share on Lead a Group.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "0Xd4RwIgWo", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Background checks for a group", "col": 12}}, {"id": "7SkJRn0DE4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "In the Requirements section of the Joining tab, tick Needs Background Check when the people in the group must be cleared, such as the leaders of a children's class. Choose the Required Checks (or none for any current, cleared check), and in Checks Apply To choose Leaders or Everyone.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "89Dcl8T4cH", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When you add a person or change their role, Churchit checks them for today. With Block People Without Checks ticked, the group cannot be saved until the person has the checks, also when a leader approves a join request. Otherwise you get a warning.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "XsoLmpEKNm", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Group files", "col": 12}}, {"id": "8Z43OZfK6v", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Group File is a file that only the members of a group can open, such as study notes. Staff add one in the desk: choose the group, type a title and upload the file with Private ticked. Leaders add one on the Group Files page of the member portal with Add a file. Members open the files of their groups on that page. Nobody outside the group can open a file, even with its link. Only staff can change or delete a file.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "60Wv8T8UhP", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Find a Group", "col": 12}}, {"id": "l5lZr1jwdg", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Find a Group page of the website lists the groups that visitors can join (active, Public and Show in Portal), with their type, description, meeting time and the city of the meeting place. Visitors filter by type and by day. A map shows each group near its meeting place, never at the exact address. A visitor signs in to join. Each group shows Member, Ask to Join, Requested, Full or Closed as it applies. Below the list is a link to the Connection Card.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "87kVygXZaf", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Lead a Group", "col": 12}}, {"id": "MPx4wI6rp4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Leaders open Lead a Group in the member portal. It shows each group that they lead: the members with the contact details that they share, the requests to join, and the meetings of the last 8 weeks.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "udukeZqY0V", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Take attendance: tick everyone who came and click Save attendance. The rest are marked absent. If the group did not meet, tick The group did not meet. A check-in from the Check-In Station stays as it is.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "RaDM9Q1gjs", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Attendance reminder: the day after a meeting with no attendance, each leader gets an email that asks them to record it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "i9aiak9Lzf", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Message the group: write a subject and a message and click Send. Each living member who allows Group Messages gets a copy, and so does the leader. When the site can send texts, the leader can choose a text instead. A leader can send 10 messages an hour.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "0cocfbiCfI", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Email Templates Group Attendance Reminder, Group Message, Group Join Request and Group Join Decision hold the text of these emails.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "PA4cIUhOsm", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Group Attendance report shows each group that met in the dates you choose (the last 12 weeks at first): the meetings held, the average attendance, the members and the attendance rate. Meetings marked Did Not Meet, future meetings and the group's schedule do not count, and only Confirmed, Assumed and Checked-In attendance counts.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "J8YYkBe4_X", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udcd4Church Directory", "col": 12}}, {"id": "iYH-sLabLc", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Church Directory is a printed (or PDF) book of your church family: each household with its photo, names, phone numbers, emails and address, and extra pages such as birthdays, groups and missionaries. Church Staff and Church Managers make it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "KgGlLR-Rp_", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Y7iX6juaWD", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example
Each fall, the church secretary prints a directory booklet for the members. She ticks Members Only, Photos and Hide Non Active People, adds the Birthday List and the Notes Page, and ticks Booklet and Page Numbers. She prints the PDF double-sided, folds the sheets in half and staples them.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "2gVSPskK3A", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Make the directory", "col": 12}}, {"id": "z2SPHJTdnF", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Open Church Directory in the People sidebar.
2. Choose the options (see below). The preview updates after each choice.
3. Click Print Directory to open the directory as a PDF, and print it from there.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ceLWmWUwxq", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "For a booklet, print double-sided, flip on the short edge, keep the sheets in order and fold them in half.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "0-ERvJdtXC", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The options", "col": 12}}, {"id": "PLf0yFypsd", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "People", "col": 12}}, {"id": "KpsR4K2lU3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Members Only: leaves out everyone who is not a member. It is off at first, so visitors and contacts print too.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "U-3umVimX5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Hide Non Active People: leaves out everyone whose Status is not Active, with their birthday, and a couple's anniversary when either is not Active. A family whose primary contact is not Active is listed by its surname only.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "KdBYFg2naV", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Group by Family (on at first): lists each family together, with the primary contact first, then the spouse, then the others. When it is off, each person is listed by name.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "2tbpyDllrm", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "People with Hide from Directory and Bulletin ticked, and people who have died, are always left out, with their birthdays and anniversaries. A family whose primary contact is left out is listed by its surname only, such as Doe Family. A family whose members are all left out is not listed.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "DSrhph4Q9j", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Show
- Photos: shows the photos.
- Positions: shows each person's church positions that they hold today.
- Membership (on at first): shows how each person is connected, such as Member or Visitor.
- Family Relationships (on at first): shows each person's relationship in the family, such as Wife or Son.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "E2mVNYr5Fz", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Contact Details (all on at first)
- Phone Numbers and Emails: each person's primary phone and email.
- Addresses: each family's primary address. A member whose own primary address differs shows it under their name.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bJniY5151s", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Extra Pages", "col": 12}}, {"id": "egdX3_48nx", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Birthday List and Anniversary List: lists near the end. A couple is listed by their own names, such as John & Mary Smith.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "wUeP5_4D93", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Missionaries: the missionaries that are not Inactive, with their people. A Sensitive missionary shows no country, email or website. The people of a listed missionary are not printed again on the family pages.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "kMcmbo0VYG", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Notes Page: a lined page for handwritten notes.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "h34vcBMwWj", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Groups
- Group List: the active groups, with each name and description.
- Group Members: the members of each group that has Show in Directory ticked.
- Member Roles: each member's role, such as John Smith | Leader.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "vt11LOTphb", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Printing", "col": 12}}, {"id": "UxJoqFMShJ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Church Image on Cover: the image of the Church, such as a logo, at the bottom of the cover.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "y84g0gR_7h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Page Numbers: numbers each page except the cover.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "870oBI0NGG", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Booklet: a half-size booklet, two pages on each side of a letter sheet, in folding order. Up to three Notes pages are added so that the page count works.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "w6XhQ2_fYZ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Blank Back Cover: an empty last page.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "wPFNtWbXHd", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The cover shows the church's name, address, website, mission statement and Church Verse from the Church record. A branch with no website prints its parent church's website.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "JbuJwkz6bR", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Other printed papers", "col": 12}}, {"id": "JdkDwLWkkD", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Open a person and click Print for the Baptism Certificate, the Membership Certificate (Letter paper, landscape) and the Member QR Card.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "8Y30zIVAOF", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udcc7Rolodex", "col": 12}}, {"id": "5dQwuu4W7r", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Rolodex is the quickest way to look someone up and get in touch, on a computer or a phone. Every person is a card, sorted by last name. People who have died get no card. Church Staff, Church People Editor and Church Manager users can open it from the sidebar, the workspace, or the Rolodex button on the People and Families lists.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AVdoU41y2_", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "", "col": 12}}, {"id": "-XC33xb6r1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Type in the search box to find a name, family, phone number or email.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "m6tm1PQpiv", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Tap a letter down the side to jump through the alphabet.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "0zdUgcrGHT", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Use the buttons on the front of a card to call, text, email or map the person.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "YSaUSIsPd8", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Tap a card to turn it over. The back shows their positions, groups, birthday and age, anniversary, membership and address, with an Open link to their record.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "tfJgeyCoxh", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Switch to Households to see one card per family.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "LyRHKy9cwS", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Click Filters to narrow the cards by membership, status, group or position (and church). Inactive people and visitors have cards too, so filter on Status to see only active people.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "nJYic2hGBV", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Save cards and act on them", "col": 12}}, {"id": "3ZAy25y1rL", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Tap the bookmark on a card to save it, for example to build a list of everyone to call this week. Saved cards gather in a tray at the bottom of the page. Your saved cards stay with your login, so a list that you build on a computer is waiting on your phone.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "xb0Js5l5dW", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "From the tray, Email writes to everyone saved (in BCC), Print prints their cards, and Clear empties the tray. Email leaves out people who do not allow email, and tells you who has no address. Save all, Email all and Print above the cards work on everyone that your search and filters show.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "JvPeqdkZcS", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Actions in the tray works on everyone saved:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "wuXyYPdzng", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Edit gives one field the same value for everyone, such as Membership. A person whose value cannot be saved, such as an envelope number that someone else has, keeps the old value, and a message says why. With 20 people or more, the change runs in the background: reload the page after a moment. To make people Inactive, use Mark Inactive, which asks for the reason.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "T2coCRK4jD", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Check In checks them in to a Function. Add to Group adds them to a group. Add Tags tags them. Assign To gives a staff member a to-do for each person.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "oMz_XNtGpH", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- New Church Email, Email Household Adults, Verify Contact Info and Print Name Tags work as in the People list (see Lists of People).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "6c7Qmz6sJe", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Open in People List opens the People list with only the saved people.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "n4IFUvO2TS", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example
The pastor wants to call everyone in the hospital or homebound this week. He saves their cards in the Rolodex on his computer. At the hospital, he opens the Rolodex on his phone, finds the saved cards in the tray and taps Call on each.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ZM0iFbGmSr", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\uddfa\ufe0fMap of Addresses", "col": 12}}, {"id": "suKDr-22XJ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Click Map of Addresses on the People workspace to see the addresses of your people on a map. Click a pin to open its address. Church Manager, Church Staff and Church People Editor users see every address. Other users see only the addresses that they added.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "9wN2yqUNn1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- When you add or change an address, Churchit sends the address text, never a name, to the OpenStreetMap search service, and fills in its position within a few seconds. If the service cannot find the address, it is not on the map: correct it and save again.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "QUGaaCdg61", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- The map shows the addresses on the current page of the list. Click 100 or 500 at the bottom to see more.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "9mJhYT8aZO", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- To keep every address on your site, clear Look Up Addresses for the Map in People Settings. Nothing is sent while it is clear, and new addresses stay off the map. The Location and Missionary forms then do not place their pins either.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "p6DchVwDmQ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- To use another OpenStreetMap server, open Geolocation Settings, set Provider to Nomatim and set the Base URL.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "yQr6iRQssC", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udce8Member Transfers", "col": 12}}, {"id": "3QS33AQpSm", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Member Transfer records a member who moves to another church, or comes from one, often with a letter of transfer between the churches. Church Manager and Church People Editor users handle transfers.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "oH9Zm3q564", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Add a Member Transfer with the person, the Direction (In or Out) and the other church.
2. Update the Status as the transfer moves on: Requested, Pending, Letter Issued, then Confirmed (or Cancelled).
3. Print the Letter of Transfer from the form when you need one.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "tE67O87mpg", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When you confirm a transfer Out, the person's Membership changes to Contact, their Status to Inactive, and their Inactive Reason to Transferred to another church. When you confirm a transfer In, the person gets a Membership life event dated that day, which names the other church, and becomes an active Member.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "T6mGT1UOe7", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "With more than one church, a move between your own branches is a transfer with a To Church: confirming it moves the person, and their member portal access, to that branch.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ol2nY7_3uv", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example
The Garcias move to another city and join a church there, which asks for a letter. The office adds an Out transfer, prints the Letter of Transfer and mails it. When the other church confirms, the office sets the status to Confirmed: the Garcias become Inactive contacts, and their history stays.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "HUiRhOApiC", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udcc8Membership Changes", "col": 12}}, {"id": "XC6pwvnPvq", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Churchit keeps a record each time a person is added, and each time their Membership or Status changes. The Membership Changes report lists these changes for a date range (the last 90 days at first), with the date, the person, the field, the old value and the new value. Use the Field and New Value filters to find, for example, everyone who became a Member this year. A person who is deleted drops out of this report.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "4j0FIImMEC", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83e\ude9cAssimilation Funnel", "col": 12}}, {"id": "2-_ZlBibi9", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Assimilation Funnel report shows how far new people go after their first visit. Set First Visit From and First Visit To (the last 3 months at first). It lists each living person whose first attended function is in those dates, with four steps:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "iCStDA3yOT", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- First Visit: every person in the list.
- Came Back: attended again within Came Back Within (Weeks) (8 at first).
- Connected: is in a group or has served on a ministry team.
- Member: became a Member since the first visit.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "k_wX3XTAr7", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A person can reach a step without the one before it. The numbers at the top and the chart show how many people reached each step.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "SV638jwZi0", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example
In the spring, 40 people visited for the first time. The funnel shows 22 came back, 9 joined a group or served, and 3 became members. The welcome team invites the people who came back but did not connect to a newcomers' lunch.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "-_ANCkJKal", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udee4\ufe0fPathways", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Epk0cuGeKR", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Pathway is a path that people take through the life of the church, such as Came Back, Joined a Group, Baptized and Serving. Each step is a smart list (see Lists of People). A person has done a step when they are on the step's list.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ad59pEOfj0", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Save a smart list for each step, for example a list of people whose Groups count is 1 or more.
2. Add a Pathway, give it a name, and add one row for each step, in the usual order, with the step's Smart List.
3. Click Open Progress, or open the Pathway Progress report and choose the pathway.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "QuEJ8xUKYB", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The report lists each living person who has done at least one step, with a tick for each step done and the first step not done yet. With more than one church, a pathway counts only the people of its own church. To start a follow-up when a person reaches a step, add an On Smart List trigger with the step's list to a Follow-up Workflow (see Follow-up).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "wq-YALy-9s", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udccbLists of People", "col": 12}}, {"id": "iw7VUGVZyF", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Much of a church office's work starts with a list: the visitors of last month, the members not seen lately, the parents of the children's class. Churchit keeps figures on each person, ships ready-made lists, and lets you save your own lists. A saved list of people is a smart list: it stays up to date by itself, and you can email it, follow it up or use it in a pathway.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fKR2pabZMp", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example
The pastor wants to call every member who has not come since Easter. The secretary opens the Person Report view, adds the filters Membership is Member and Last Attended is before Easter Sunday, and saves it as Not Seen Since Easter. The list updates itself each day. A week later she opens it again: two people who came back on Sunday are no longer on it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fxPTZRkQ4v", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Figures on each person", "col": 12}}, {"id": "K2Q8NHWjjW", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Connections tab of the Person form shows figures that Churchit keeps up to date from other records, so you can filter people on them:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Y_0G1TLrOu", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Involvement: First Attended, Last Attended and Times Attended (90 Days) count attendance that is Confirmed, Assumed or Checked-In. Last Served and Times Served (90 Days) count accepted serving assignments. Groups and Group Count show the active groups the person is in.
