Ministry Teams and Team Positions list the person's serving teams.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "VBvd3YyJEs", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Giving: First Gift, Last Gift and Lapsed Giver (see the Finances manual). Only Church Finance, Church Manager and System Manager users see these.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "R_sbWlOAQX", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Care: Open Care Requests, Last Visited (the latest completed visit), and the most recent Background Check with its expiry. Only Church Pastoral Care, Church Manager and System Manager users see these.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "jZyNxCkJ7n", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Membership Changed On and Status Changed On: the dates that the Membership and the Status last changed.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "5MUiHpZJPA", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The figures change soon after a record is saved, and again every night. They count the records of the person's own church and the shared records.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "QFCt5MxR1h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Standard lists", "col": 12}}, {"id": "sjFP726X-u", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Churchit ships these lists. Open them from the folders of the People sidebar. No list shows people who have died. You cannot change a standard list: to keep your own version, change the filters or columns, then click Save As.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "3HmGBLspd3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Inactivity Candidates: active people who attended before but not in the last 90 days.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "7vFyR46aKY", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- First-Time Visitors: people who first attended in the last 30 days and are not Members.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "HhsXCGeSrs", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Not in a Group: active adults in no group.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "-5V5NGu-8E", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Children: all children.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "589BGrjkNJ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Background Checks Expiring: cleared checks that expire in the next 30 days.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ovfpc2sJP7", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Lapsed Givers: people who gave in the last year but not in the last 90 days (finance staff and managers only).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "3W8IDTtKDb", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- People with Open Care Requests, Members Not Seen Lately and Members by Last Visit: for pastoral care staff and managers.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "2x-GNRdgho", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Inactivity Candidates and First-Time Visitors cards on the People workspace count the people on these lists in your church.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "WqRNkCZUmd", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Make your own list", "col": 12}}, {"id": "690IxwMWsX", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Open the Person Report view. It opens on Status Active: clear that filter first if the list should include everyone.
2. Click Filter and add conditions, for example Status is Active and Times Attended (90 Days) is 0.
3. To change the columns, click ..., then Pick Columns.
4. Click ..., then Save As, and type a name.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "2pu8gpju_t", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Saving a list needs the Report Manager role, which the Church Manager role profile has (a Church Branch Manager does not). A saved list is open to every staff role that can read people: to limit who sees it, change its Roles in the Report list. To open it again, pick it under Saved Reports in the Person Report view.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "jyC6TW3eAw", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Some filters that are useful:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "9O6uuJRmv9", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- People on the Welcome team: Ministry Teams (Person Ministry Team) Ministry equals Welcome.
- People who became members in 2025: Membership equals Member, and Membership Changed On between January 1 and December 31, 2025.
- People baptized in 2025: Life Event (Life Event) Event Type equals Baptism, and Life Event Date in 2025.
- People with a skill: Skill (Person Skill) equals the skill.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "z_s25alECb", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Get a list by email. A Church Manager opens the list, clicks ..., then Setup Auto Email, and adds an Auto Email Report with who gets it, how often and in which format. Keep Send only if there is any data ticked. The email shows only the people that the chosen user may see.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "uAXPF2mUzl", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Attendance count lists", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bSJJe8_77I", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Attendance Count report lists the people who attended at least a number of times since a date (1 time in the last 3 months at first). You can also set Until and a Function Type.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "x1NvI36mx5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To use it as a smart list, open the menu at the top right, click Save and give it a name. The saved list counts again each time it is used. It counts only Confirmed, Assumed and Checked-In attendance at functions that have started, of the person's own church and shared functions.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "3t3F6dgv7l", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example
To find the regulars who are not members yet, save an Attendance Count with Since three months ago and At Least 8 times. Use it as the Smart List of a Church Email that invites them to the next membership class.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "b1YoGl53Tg", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Act on a list", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ZQ5A3dwOwe", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Tick people in the Person list or a saved list, then open Actions:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "zlfXI2kKz2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- New Church Email starts a Church Email to them (see the Communications manual).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "SMARAq5Qgw", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Email opens your own mail app with their addresses in BCC. Email Household Adults writes to the Adults of their households, for example the parents of a list of children. Both leave out people who do not allow email, and tell you who.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "BK2-xmLziV", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Add to Group, Add Tags, Assign To, Edit and Mark Inactive (with the Inactive Reason) change them all at once.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "syJDjUehtY", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Check In checks them in to a Function. Print Name Tags prints their tags. Verify Contact Info starts Contact Verification cards.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "qhuTWcOsvq", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Open in Rolodex shows only them in the Rolodex.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "uaKPqWJuGo", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "In the Family list, Actions, then Email, writes to each household at its own email address.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "8_bPa9aIU1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Mailing labels", "col": 12}}, {"id": "4RFhU4xoG6", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Tick people or families, then click Actions, then Print. Choose Mailing Label in the Person list, or Household Label in the Family list (addressed like John & Jane Smith).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "yURBYsLebL", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Each label prints on its own 3.5 x 1.125 inch page, for a roll label printer such as a DYMO LabelWriter (30252 labels) or a Brother QL (DK-1201 labels). A label skips an address marked Returned and uses the family's address when the person has none. The country prints only when it is not your church's country.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AYPRprZlVp", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Lists with AI", "col": 12}}, {"id": "pSuqwbK9PH", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When AI is turned on (see the Foundations manual):", "col": 12}}, {"id": "N-o1U5wXT-", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Describe People: in the Person list menu, choose Describe People, type who you want, such as \"members who have not attended in 2 months and are not in a group\", and click Find. Churchit shows how many people match and each filter in plain words. Read the filters: the AI can write filters that look right and are wrong. Click Apply Filters, then save the list as above. The AI gets your words and the names of your fields and choices, never a person.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "qHgZWr2ecp", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- An AI app or the Church Office agent can give you a list link from your words (open it, and remove any filter left from your last visit that your words did not ask for), answer the weekly questions of the office (first-time guests with no follow-up, people not seen lately, birthdays this week, groups that need attention, open serving positions), and brief you on a person or a group before a visit.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "uDh-UTFLgp", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "It shows only what you may read in the desk. A briefing can hold care and giving details that you may read, so prefer a local AI model for it, and do not share an AI chat that holds a briefing.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "s0W4lUjOrP", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Brief Me: on a Person or Group form, click View, then Brief Me, for a short summary of what you may read, with links to its sources. It is not saved, and it holds no judgment or advice. Medical notes, allergies and emergency contacts are never sent. Check the timeline before you act.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Z-4t3iWYn_", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83e\uddf9Clean Data", "col": 12}}, {"id": "rD3pmCogOK", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A church's records get untidy over time: the same person entered twice, an email with a typo, a family that moved. Churchit finds these problems for you, and Contact Verification cards let people correct their own details.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "lAU5KcFdNU", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Possible Duplicates", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fWE2NnoiLg", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When you add a person and type a first name and an email or phone, Churchit compares them with the people already there. If the new person may already exist, a yellow note at the top of the form links to each match with the reasons. The note does not stop you from saving.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "a0Mla_rDUd", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Each week, Churchit also looks for living people in the same church who may be the same person, and adds each pair to the Possible Duplicates list (Open Possible Duplicates on the workspace). It does not pair people in the same family, and it does not add a pair again after someone closes it. Imports and first portal sign-ins add pairs too.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "4hcDljtLJe", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Open a pair to see the two people side by side. A gray row has the same value for both.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "gWw5Hjy0Dz", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Click Merge to make them one person (see Merge two records of one person). Only users who can delete people, such as a Church Manager, see it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "jHlu1-WQfU", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Click Not a Duplicate when they are different people. Churchit does not pair them again. A Church People Editor can do this.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "eZUIA9WziS", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Each pair has a score from 0 to 100. The same email, phone, birth date and name raise it, and a different first name, birth date, gender or suffix (such as Jr. and Sr.) lowers it. Churchit knows common nicknames, so Bob and Robert can be the same person. A pair must reach the Duplicate Match Threshold in People Settings (80 at first). A higher number finds fewer pairs.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "GK_oaQMBYG", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example
Robert Jones filled in a Connection Card as \"Bob Jones\" with his phone number. The weekly scan pairs Bob Jones with Robert Jones, score 80, because the phone and the last name match and Bob is a nickname of Robert. The office opens the pair, clicks Merge and keeps Robert's record.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "y-H4Y7bPKr", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When AI is turned on, View, then Explain Match, on a pair explains in a few sentences why the two may be one person, and which value of each field to keep. AI never merges people.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "1ZwWjxy0Za", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Find a person by phone or email", "col": 12}}, {"id": "VvWerjYQua", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "In any field where you choose a person, you can type a name, a nickname, a phone number (four or more digits, in any format) or an email address (with its @ sign).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "WelKtL5RM4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "People Data Quality report", "col": 12}}, {"id": "YYM-D0RRl7", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The People Data Quality report shows living people whose records need attention, one problem on each row: No Way to Reach (no email, phone or address on the person or the family), Invalid Email, Invalid Phone Number, Email Bounced, Mail Returned, Possible Duplicate, Child Without Birth Date and No Family. Use the Problem filter to see one problem at a time. No Family shows only when you choose it. Church Manager and Church People Editor users can open it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Y6X7lHLBmx", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When mail sent to an address comes back, tick Returned on that address. When email comes back, Churchit ticks Bounced by itself (see the Communications manual).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "SMqB4u8sNc", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When AI is turned on, Suggest Fixes on the report suggests corrections for invalid emails and phone numbers. It sends only those values, never names. The boxes start empty: check each suggestion, tick the ones that are right and click Save Ticked.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "h2odjXpYkc", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Contact Verification cards", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bkQurqu5sT", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Contact Verification prints a card for each person with what the church has on file: emails, phones, addresses, birthday and more, with their photo and a QR code. The person ticks Right or Wrong on each line, writes corrections, fills in what is blank and signs the card. Two cards print on each Letter page.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "WfmZJamuFv", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example
Before the new directory, the office makes a Contact Verification for the Women's Bible Study group and prints the cards. The leader hands each woman her own card. The next week the cards come back. The secretary scans each QR code with her phone, types the corrections, and clicks Save Card. Three women update their details online instead with the second QR code.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "yiuZagfAV9", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Open Contact Verifications in the Data folder, click Add Contact Verification and give it a title.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "7YqVBe8IcR", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "2. Pick a Group to add its living members when you save, or add people to the People table. With more than one church, the people must belong to the church of the Contact Verification. You can also tick people in the People list and click Actions, then Verify Contact Info.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "1r2FZBqsh9", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "3. Under Show on the Cards, tick what the cards show. After the first card comes back, these ticks cannot change.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ljevnNpSAu", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "4. Save, then click Print.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "eClBRqKkM4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Give each card to its own person, because the card shows their contact details. Church Manager and Church People Editor users make Contact Verifications.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "0qkJiP4oc_", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Record a returned card. Scan the QR code on the card with a phone while you are signed in, or click Scan Card or Record Returned Card and pick the person. The window shows what the church has on file. Change what the person corrected, add what they wrote, and tick Remove on a line marked Wrong with nothing written beside it. Click Save Card.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "lGWrRSadXa", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Churchit changes the person, records their answer about text messages as a consent, and sets Contact Verified On on the person. The card's row then shows Confirmed or Updated. A change to a family address changes it for the whole household. An email or phone that another person already has can be shared only within one family: for anyone else, Save Card stops and names that person. To print again for the cards that did not come back, tick Print Only Cards Not Returned.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ceqj73sjKT", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Update online. When Update Online Code is ticked, each card also prints an Or update online QR code. It opens the Update Your Details page with no login (see Send Details Link), where the person can change everything except their addresses. Their row then shows Answered Online. The link works once, until 30 days after Handed Out On.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "xCoKIWWe39", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To give more time, change Handed Out On, save and print the cards that did not come back again. Untick Update Online Code to end the links that were not used. Anyone who finds a lost card can use its link, so give each card to its own person.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "H9iBQTDtON", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When AI is turned on, Read Card with AI in the Returned Card window fills in the window from a photo of the card. Check each value against the card before you save. A card that shows the emergency contact is never read with AI.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "lbc02cFC4R", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udce5Import People", "col": 12}}, {"id": "UaNQUIbjzK", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When your church moves to Churchit, you can bring your people from another church system or from a spreadsheet. Churchit makes a Person for each row and a Family for each household, and keeps the ID that each person had in the old system. When you import a newer file from the same system, Churchit updates those people instead of adding them again. Church Managers and System Managers can import people.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fBflyMlYJ5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Each import goes through Frappe's Data Import tool, in the Data folder of the People sidebar. It reads the file, shows a preview and adds the people in the background.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "8J0iQrTWBS", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example
Your church used Planning Center. You export the people as a CSV file, make a Data Import with the type Planning Center Import, and upload the file. The preview asks you to map the Name Prefix \"Mr.\" to Mr. After the import, 350 people and 140 families are in Churchit, and Possible Duplicates lists 4 pairs to check.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "9cTD7-It92", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Import from Planning Center", "col": 12}}, {"id": "RtB9JPxwD1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. In Planning Center People, open the gear menu and click Import & Export CSV, then Start Export. Download the CSV file from the email (open the ZIP file if needed).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ystn0hPRYe", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "2. In Churchit, open Data Imports in the Data folder and click Add Data Import. Set Document Type to Planning Center Import.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "G-vlW102Eo", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "3. For the first import, keep Import Type as Insert New Records. For a later import, choose Insert or Update Records.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ECpOFRfFD2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "4. Save, upload the file without changing it, and click Next.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "_pxXVEtSbo", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "5. Map each value that Churchit does not know to a value of your church, or skip its rows.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "VbUhoe7FfO", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "6. Click Import.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "aLJb5yYHmR", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Household Primary Contact becomes the family's Primary Contact. A person with Child set is a Child, and the others are Adults.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "BBTwxTDC-W", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Import from Rock RMS", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Uzu9RYyaJ6", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Rock RMS cannot export all people at once, so make a report once and export it each time.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "-iyZ3J5Dpy", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. In Rock, open Tools, then Reports, and add a report for the Person entity.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "dH2FFsmzi5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "2. Add these fields, with each Column Header set to the name here: Id, Family Id (the Primary Family Id field), Family Name, Family Role (the Age Classification field), Title, First Name, Nick Name, Middle Name, Last Name, Suffix, Gender, Birthdate, Anniversary Date, Marital Status, Connection Status, Record Status, Inactive Reason, Is Deceased, Email, Mobile Phone, Home Phone, Work Phone, Home Address Street 1, Home Address Street 2, Home Address City, Home Address State, Home Address Postal Code and Home Address Country. Id, Family Id and First Name are required.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "mP3AaATP0C", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "3. Run the report and click Export to Excel.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "WHyJQeV4Vk", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "4. In Churchit, add a Data Import with Document Type Rock RMS Import, as for Planning Center.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "vvWZxoRbR9", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "5. Map the values that Churchit does not know, for example the Connection Status Attendee to Regular Attender, and click Import.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "KtzxX1b_d7", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Rock has no head of household, so Churchit makes the first Adult of each family its Primary Contact. You can change it on the Family.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "YQNJeJ32K2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Import from Breeze", "col": 12}}, {"id": "BsaYxyexXt", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. In Breeze, click the gear icon, then Manage Account, View More and Export. Choose People and download the spreadsheet.
2. Make sure that the Birthdate column uses the format mm/dd/yyyy.
3. In Churchit, add a Data Import with Document Type Breeze Import, as for Planning Center, and upload the file without other changes.
4. Map each Status to a Membership, for example Attender to Regular Attender, and click Import.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "2VQIWGsAsD", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Head of Household becomes the Primary Contact. A Child is a Child, and a Spouse or Adult is an Adult. For other people, Churchit uses the age: an adult age makes an Other Adult. Set the remaining roles on the Family.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "qiXxUKb-6W", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Import from a spreadsheet", "col": 12}}, {"id": "T_NW1mcUOd", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Add a Data Import with Document Type People Import, save, and click Download Template. The usual columns are ticked. Tick more if you need them, such as Envelope Number or Medical Notes.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "8n8jJA_ose", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "2. Put one person on each row, with a Person ID. Give the people of one household the same Household ID. Set Primary Contact to Yes for one person of each household, and Household Role to Adult, Other Adult or Child.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "V8Jb5fcvMk", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "3. If the people come from another system, type its name in Imported From.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "w_Q_UZz1P_", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "4. Upload the file, check the preview and click Import.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "T6H_azfyB1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The preview and after the import", "col": 12}}, {"id": "iWbfZ9x9i5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- A row that cannot be imported stops the import, for example a row with no first name, or an address with a country that Churchit does not know. Correct the file, or click Skip Row. A value that Churchit does not know stops the import until you map it. A note, such as an invalid email that Churchit leaves out, does not stop it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "X5dlaJue-c", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- The same person twice in a file is imported once, with a note.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "JQdG45D2Tz", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- An update changes only the fields that have a value in the file. It adds new emails, phones and addresses and keeps the old ones. Update Existing Records updates only people imported before.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "KqC3BIMmTQ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Each imported person has the Source Import, and Imported From and Imported ID show where they came from.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "3O28bYAJGF", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Churchit compares each new person with the people already there and adds Possible Duplicates. Review them and merge the people who are the same.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "P_CDikSnWp", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When AI is turned on, Suggest Mapping at the top right of a Data Import matches the headings that Churchit does not know to its fields. Only the headings go to the AI, never a row. Check each pair, click Use This Mapping, and save.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "6wmO9kqy95", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Undo an import", "col": 12}}, {"id": "CXfwVB4EKX", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To remove the people and families that one import added, for example after an import with wrong columns, do it soon, before people add attendance or gifts to the new records. You need the right to delete people and families, which a Church Manager has.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "7iA7caFDVY", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Open the People list and filter on Source equals Import, Imported From equals the system, and Created On the day of the import. Make sure the list shows everyone (click 500 at the bottom).
2. Tick the box in the list header to select all, click Actions, then Delete, and confirm.
3. Do the same in the Families list.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "pvMOf-FmJW", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Frappe does not delete a person that a later record names, such as someone who attended a function after the import, and it does not delete a family that still has a person. It lists what it did not delete.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Z55p79eC51", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "More than 10 records are deleted in the background, with a message when it is done. The addresses of deleted families stay in the Address list, where a System Manager can delete them.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fhpyqkWZbW", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Undoing an update import
The undo does not change back the people that an update import changed.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "uNkH0u-isC", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\ude4bConnection Cards", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ZbbipjkPhM", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Connection Card is the welcome card that a guest fills in on their phone, at /connection-card on your website. They give their name, email and phone, say whether they are new, tick what they would like to do next, and add the people who came with them. Churchit then adds them to People and starts their follow-up, so that no guest is forgotten.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "7Lexiqa-0I", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "", "col": 12}}, {"id": "2P9i_aWjlw", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example
On Sunday, the Lees scan the QR code in the bulletin and fill in a card: Daniel and Grace Lee, with their son Sam, age 7, and a tick on \"Join a group\". Churchit adds the three as Visitors in one Lee family, and starts a follow-up card on the Welcome workflow and on the Groups workflow. On Monday, the welcome volunteer sees the card on her board and calls them.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "EEVH-dpHpX", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "What happens to a card", "col": 12}}, {"id": "c8YR7i5fw6", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "After a guest sends a card, Churchit looks for them in People:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "KGWxtmQoos", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- If one person has the same email or phone and the same first and last name, the card is linked to that person. Churchit does not change that person's details, and does not add the people who came with them.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "95JEXUSpF8", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- If not, Churchit adds the guest as a new person with the Membership Visitor and the Source Connection Card, with How They Heard from the card. Close matches go to Possible Duplicates for you to check.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "V5U1ij8_Gq", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Then each follow-up workflow that starts on a Connection Card opens a follow-up card for the person (see Follow-up).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "u04JkSQN6X", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The list shows each card's status: New until Churchit finds or adds the person, Processed, or Spam. On a processed card, Person opens the person it was linked to or added, and Connections shows the follow-up cards it started. Church Manager and Church People Editor users can also add a card in the desk from a paper card, and Churchit handles it the same way.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ylJ8DQ5XcG", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "What guests can tick", "col": 12}}, {"id": "CD-air0SDA", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The boxes under I Would Like To come from the Connection Card Interest list: Join a group, Serve on a team, Learn about salvation, Learn about baptism, Learn about membership and Talk with a pastor at first. You can rename, delete or add your own. To start a workflow when a guest ticks one, add a Connection Card trigger with that interest to the workflow.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ydp-XBC-hl", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Stay in Touch boxes, Email Me Church News and Events and Text Me Church News and Events, record the guest's yes to Church News (see Consent in the Communications manual).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "d9f5dyjshZ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Who came with the guest", "col": 12}}, {"id": "LgGtuUEqH9", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "In Who Is With You? a guest can add the people who came with them: name, relationship and birth date. When Churchit adds the guest as a new Visitor, it makes a family with the guest as the Primary Contact, and adds each of these people to it as a Visitor.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "M0WFM2TO1f", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A person with no last name gets the guest's last name. A Wife or Husband becomes the guest's spouse. A birth date becomes a Birth life event, so the family can set each household role.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "zozONgkgCT", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Print a QR code for the form", "col": 12}}, {"id": "golcRHjtIP", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Open the Connection Card web form and click QR Code. With more than one church, choose the church that the cards are for. Click Download to save the code for your bulletin or welcome card. Every published web form has this button, so you can do the same for the prayer request form.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "-bEe_cy1Ir", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Spam and busy Sundays", "col": 12}}, {"id": "NJJZeTb1hM", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The form has a box that people never see but robots fill in. A card with that box filled in gets the status Spam and adds nobody. If a real guest's card was marked Spam, add the person yourself.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Dt8SVLtW3d", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Each internet address can send the form at most 10 times a minute. On a busy Sunday, guests on the church Wi-Fi share one address. A guest who sees \"too many requests\" can send the card again a minute later.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "6HUSCKihlT", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Paper connection cards", "col": 12}}, {"id": "_oUFMkEeXU", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "For a paper card, add a photo of it and type the card from the photo:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "3u9K4s4UHM", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Open Connection Card Photos (Card Photos in the sidebar) and click Add. You need the Church People Editor or Church Manager role.
2. Attach one clear photo of one card, taken from above, and save. The photo is a private file.
3. Click Copy by Hand. A new Connection Card opens with the photo at the top. Type what the card shows and save. The photo then shows Imported, and the follow-up starts as for any card.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ucJN5KRpn3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When AI is turned on (see the Foundations manual) and the site has Flow, AI reads the photo into a draft instead. The status goes from Waiting to Reading to Ready to Check. Compare each value of the draft with the photo, because AI can misread handwriting, then click Create Connection Card, correct the card and save it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "eNDE7Qd8Fr", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "AI never ticks Email Me or Text Me, and adds no person by itself. When AI cannot read a photo, the status is Failed: click Actions, then Read Again. A card holds children's names, so AI reads a photo only with a model that keeps no copy of your data. When AI is off, a new photo is Ready to Copy.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "3fL3RatBIT", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Delete a photo that you do not use when you are done with it. Deleting a Connection Card deletes its photo too.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "YJNidGa-eg", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83e\uddedFollow-up", "col": 12}}, {"id": "RwTDaJZSoT", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Follow-up makes sure that each person who needs a next step gets one: a first-time guest gets a welcome call, a new member gets a coffee invitation, a person who asked about baptism hears from the pastor. A Follow-up Workflow is the list of steps, and a Follow-up Card is one person moving through those steps, on a board like sticky notes on a wall.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "cp5l7iD725", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "", "col": 12}}, {"id": "DCTv_KqoG_", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example
The Welcome workflow has three steps: Welcome Call (Sarah, 2 days), Coffee Invitation (the pastor, 7 days) and Connect to a Group (Tom, 14 days). When a guest's Connection Card arrives, a card opens at Welcome Call and Sarah gets a to-do and an email. After her call, she drags the card to Coffee Invitation, and the pastor gets the next to-do. When the guest has joined a group, Tom closes the card with the outcome \"Joined Tuesday Bible Study\".", "col": 12}}, {"id": "2jwose61O9", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Make a workflow", "col": 12}}, {"id": "CtgnArtF-l", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Open Follow-up Workflows and click Add Follow-up Workflow. Give it a name.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "CYKdUoZITm", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "2. On the Details tab, add one row in Steps for each step, in order. In Assign To, choose who takes the step, and in Due In (Days), how many days they have. A step with no user is assigned to nobody, and Churchit warns you when you save.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ih3tpDAE08", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "3. On the Automation tab, choose what starts a card (see below) and any actions.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ZGnHgEPX0K", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "4. Tick Active and save.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "a1pgiNesHM", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When you save, Churchit makes a board with a column for each step. Click Open Board to see it. You cannot remove a step while open cards are on it. Only Church Managers add and change workflows.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AFGefFxQDX", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When AI is turned on (see the Foundations manual), Describe the Process on a new workflow drafts the steps, triggers and actions from your words, such as \"Call a first-time guest in 2 days, invite them for coffee after 5 days, and send a welcome email\". Check the draft, pick Assign To for each step, and turn on Active when it is ready.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "9X--906_zZ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Follow-up cards and the board", "col": 12}}, {"id": "6y1J9xNFqX", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "See the diagram in the online manual", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ad1ueu3oIS", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Follow-up Card shows the person's phone and email, the step, and when it is due. A person can have only one open card on a workflow. When two records of one person are merged, only the older open card on each workflow stays open. To add a card by hand, open the person, go to Connections and click + next to Follow-up Card.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "8XbS7vbkcz", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Move: drag the card to the next column on the board, or open it and click Move To. The person of the new step gets a to-do and one email, and the due date starts again.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "hCpLdLdpDu", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Snooze: hides a card until a date, 7 days at first. It comes back by itself.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "erJ9AQ7IUQ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Close: when the follow-up is done. Write what happened in Outcome. Closing also closes the to-do.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "kTtNzCbm84", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Follow-up Cards list opens on the open cards, the soonest due first. Clear the Status filter to see closed cards. A card that a Connection Card started shows the interests the guest ticked and the guest's message as its reason.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "6ccvJn6KoY", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Start cards by themselves", "col": 12}}, {"id": "izgRKRp3FS", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "On the Automation tab, under Start a Card When, add a row for each event that should start a card. Leave Which blank to start on any value, or choose one:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "guV2kHHhK9", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Connection Card: a guest sends a card. Which is the interest they ticked.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "KmnuDUMM9y", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- First Check-In: a person checks in for the first time ever (volunteer check-ins do not count). Which is the Function Type.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "O7wu777GGO", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Signed Up: a sign-up becomes Confirmed. Which is the Function Type. A card starts for each attendee who has a Person.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "q58k6xtyN5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Form Submitted: a person sends a form. Which is the Question Set.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "qseHJ_OPrD", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Life Event Added: a life event is added, for example a Baptism.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "nmgpN02pzf", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Membership Type Becomes and Member Status Becomes: a person's membership or status changes to this value.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "0ji2MEIU57", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- On Smart List: once a day, everyone new on a saved list gets a card, each person only once.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "miqxxGsyii", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Step Reached and Card Closed: a card on another workflow reaches a step (type the Step, or leave it empty for every step) or closes. The new card shows the first card as its Source. A workflow cannot start itself, and it can start only from a workflow of the same church.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "oQQsf7BXnm", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "If the person already has an open card on the workflow, no second card starts. For a shared function or form, the person's own church does the follow-up.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "7HwsLzTVkU", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example
When a Welcome card closes, you want new members to get a Membership Class card. Add a trigger Card Closed with Which set to Welcome on the Membership Class workflow.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "-vGXqIY6CN", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Actions on a workflow", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ZdtCifqGHh", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A workflow can do work by itself when a card opens, reaches a step or closes. On the Automation tab, add a row in Actions. In When, choose Card Opened, Step Reached (with its Step, or empty for every step) or Card Closed. In Action, choose:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "cpIjbUMpIy", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Send Email: choose a Purpose and an Email Template.
- Send Text: choose a Purpose and type the Text Message.
- Add to Group: choose a Group of your church.
- Add Tag: choose a Tag.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "IxH9Veh5Go", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A message can use {{ first_name }}, {{ last_name }}, {{ display_name }}, {{ full_name }} and {{ step }}. A workflow with any other placeholder cannot be saved. A message goes only to a person who allows the Purpose, and a text only to a person who said yes to texts. Each action runs once for each card, event and step.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "x22-LiPrPT", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To see what ran, open the Connections tab of the workflow, or Follow-up Action Runs in the Setup folder. Done means the action ran, Skipped that there was nothing to do (for example the person has no address or is already in the group), and Failed shows the error. A failed action does not run again.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "xlgWFpv6a2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Follow-up volunteers", "col": 12}}, {"id": "wImX86eFDI", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Give a volunteer the Church Follow-up Team role profile. A volunteer sees only the cards assigned to them, on the board and in the list, and can move, snooze and close those cards. After they move or close a card, they can open it but not change it. After they sign in, the volunteer opens Follow-up Cards.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "FH9giOb3ml", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Church People Editor and Church Pastoral Care users add and change any card.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "VKD6Yj3Ex6", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Reminders and notices", "col": 12}}, {"id": "j74z6KeVZb", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- On any card, click ..., then Remind Me, to get a reminder at a time you pick, or Follow to get an email when the card changes (turn on Send Notifications For Documents Followed By Me in your user settings).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "18ZIplDXpR", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- To email the person assigned to an overdue card, a Church Manager ticks Email When a Follow-up Card Is Overdue under Reminders in People Settings. Days After the Card Is Due sets when (1 day at first). Snoozed cards get no email.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "wqkSshnX_E", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- The shipped Visitor Follow-Up notification can email the Church Managers about each new visitor (see Notifications in the Communications manual).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "mKz2C0eStC", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "AI suggestion on a new card", "col": 12}}, {"id": "0D_sJGVZDv", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When AI is turned on and a Church Manager has turned on suggestions on new requests (see the Foundations manual), a new card that a Connection Card or a form started gets a comment AI suggestion: which workflow fits, why, and a first email. Click Draft the Email to open a new Church Email to the person, not saved: read it, change it and send it yourself. AI never moves the card or sends a message.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "oEt_IcLz_u", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83e\udd1dCare Requests", "col": 12}}, {"id": "1kfsRuM0hV", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Care Request records that someone needs practical help: meals after a surgery, a hospital visit, a ride, help after a death. It tracks who takes care of it and when it must be done, so nobody falls through the cracks. Members can ask for care in the member portal, and staff add requests in the desk.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "U99NLjEWqN", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "", "col": 12}}, {"id": "_z_LMdr9vU", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Church Pastoral Care and Church Manager users handle care requests. Church Staff can add and read them.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "wVdDVAxB2P", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example
Ruth Brown asks for meals after her hip surgery, in the member portal. Her Care Assignment names Deacon Mike as her caregiver, so the request goes on Mike's To Do list, due in 7 days, and he gets an email. Mike moves the card to In Progress on the Care Board, arranges a week of meals with the Hospitality team, writes what was done in Resolution Notes, and sets the request to Resolved.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "n-S4dC2FD3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Add a care request", "col": 12}}, {"id": "gd6hmVl_py", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Open Care Requests and click Add Care Request.
2. Pick the Person that the request is for. Caregiver fills in from their Care Assignment (see below). You can change it.
3. Choose the Type, such as Meals or Hospital Visit, and the Urgency. You can add more Care Request Types.
4. Describe the need and save.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "oN37lmfK4I", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Due On is set from the urgency: Urgent 1 day, High 3 days, Medium 7 days, Low 14 days. When you change the urgency, the due date is counted again. You can also type a date, but not one before Submitted On. A request from the member portal starts with Medium urgency.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Va3rc0iXcH", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Who is told", "col": 12}}, {"id": "CxOfobcgkw", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- When the caregiver has a desk login, the request goes on their To Do list, dated when it is due, and they get an email. When you choose a new caregiver, the request moves to that person's list. When you resolve or close it, it leaves the list.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "-PuwDVGZHu", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- When there is no caregiver with a desk login, the Church Pastoral Care users and the Church Managers of the church get an email and a desk notification (New Care Request). A caregiver with no desk login gets nothing, and Churchit tells you so: let them know yourself.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "w3jOQR6HbT", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- To email the caregiver and the care team when a request is overdue, a Church Manager ticks Email When a Care Request Is Overdue under Reminders in People Settings. Days After the Request Is Due sets when (1 day at first).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "cuPl1rPDTH", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- The member who asked sees the status of their request in the member portal, and it updates when staff change it. Only staff can change the status.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "loizs6THGd", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Status and the Care Board", "col": 12}}, {"id": "CWavUbeuAP", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A request moves through Requested, Triaged (someone has looked at it), In Progress, Resolved and Closed. The Care Requests list opens on the requests that are not Resolved or Closed, the soonest due first. Clear the Status filter to see all.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "MTjeWXQN7_", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Care Board shows the open requests as cards in a column for each status. Drag a card to another column to change its status. Open it from the Care Board shortcut on the People workspace, or choose Kanban in the view menu of the list. Write what was done in Resolution Notes. Reopening a resolved request puts it back on the caregiver's To Do list.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "4rQsGe0M3r", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Churchit keeps a history of changes to care requests, care assignments, visits and member transfers, in Activity at the bottom of the form. With more than one church, the caregiver must be able to see the request's church.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bWei6rO-7x", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "AI suggestions. When AI is turned on and a Church Manager has turned on suggestions on new requests (see the Foundations manual), a new care request shows an AI Suggestion part with a suggested category and urgency to the care team. Use Category and Use Urgency fill in the form without saving it. The AI never replies or chooses the caregiver.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "G58VOk2-wQ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udc65Care Assignments", "col": 12}}, {"id": "91-sVTulaM", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Care Assignment gives a person a caregiver for a time, such as a deacon or an elder who looks after a group of households. When you pick that person on a Care Request, Caregiver fills in from their current assignment.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "pRsh18I_Bd", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Add a Care Assignment with the person, the caregiver and the start date. Leave the end date empty for no end. The list shows each assignment as Current, Upcoming (before its start date) or Ended (after its end date). Click one to see only those.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "UDyYB1kk4o", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example
The church divides its families among six deacons. Each family's members get a Care Assignment to their deacon. When one of them asks for a meal, the request goes straight to the right deacon.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "PiH3ReqEth", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udeaaVisitations", "col": 12}}, {"id": "-MkUe6c4bv", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Visitation Log records a visit to a person by someone from the church: a hospital visit, a home visit, a welcome visit. It holds the Person, the Visit Date, the Visit Type, who visited (Visited By), the Status, the Duration, Follow-Up Needed and notes. Only Church Pastoral Care and Church Manager users can open visitation logs.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Dj2Fgg3jRk", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Open Visitations and click Add Visitation Log.
2. Pick the person, the date and the type, and who visits. You can add more Visit Types.
3. Set the Status: Planned, Scheduled or Completed.
4. After the visit, write what happened and tick Follow-Up Needed if someone should visit again.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "P4W8gdgyFf", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- When Email Before a Planned Visit is on under Reminders in People Settings, a Planned or Scheduled visit emails the visitor and the Church Managers before the visit. Days Before the Visit sets when (1 day at first).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Wi24cpnF1_", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- With Follow-Up Needed ticked, Schedule Follow Up on the form opens a new Scheduled visit for the same person, type and visitor.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "hRJbM0bVzd", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- A visit that needs a follow-up stays on the Follow-ups Needed list until the person has a newer Scheduled or Completed visit.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "IPS8JL-EWW", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- A person's latest completed visit shows as Last Visited on their Person form. Print a list of visits with the Visitation Schedule print format.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "2fG4Tf_98U", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Pastoral Care Watch List. This report, in the Care folder, lists the people who may need a pastor now: people with a visit in the last 30 days that needs a follow-up and has nothing newer, and people with an open urgent prayer request. It shows their phone and email. Change Window (Days) to look further back.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "YpcYv50Bmf", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example
The pastor visits Mr. Jones in hospital and ticks Follow-Up Needed. Mr. Jones appears on the Watch List. The pastor clicks Schedule Follow Up for next Tuesday, and Mr. Jones leaves the Follow-ups Needed list.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "gKw7AS7OV9", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udee1\ufe0fBackground Checks", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ydonIrpgz-", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Background Check records a screening that a person had, so that leaders know who is cleared to serve, for example with children. Churchit does not run the check: order it from your provider, then record the result here. Church Pastoral Care and Church Manager users handle background checks.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "iN3eIwSMps", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Open Background Checks and click Add Background Check.
2. Pick the person and the Background Check Type: Criminal Background, Sex Offender Registry, Child Abuse Clearance, Driving Record, Child Safety Training, or your own.
3. Note the provider and their reference number, and attach the report if you have it.
4. Move the Status from Requested to Pending to Cleared or Not Cleared. A result needs a Completed On date.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "rHrE1z8OsI", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Expires On fills in from the type's Valid For (Years): Criminal Background, Sex Offender Registry and Driving Record 3 years, Child Abuse Clearance 5, Child Safety Training 2. A type with 0 years never expires. You can change the date. Each night, a cleared check past its date becomes Expired.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "mKV33LBJS_", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- The person's form shows their latest check: a cleared one on the Connections tab, and one that is Requested, Pending, Not Cleared or Expired at the top of the form, above the tabs.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "6BP5Y6JB05", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- A ministry team position or a group can require some check types and block people without them (see the Ministries manual and Group above). They accept any current cleared check of the right type.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "0L660kqCwx", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- The Checks Expiring list (in the Care folder) shows the cleared checks that expire in the next 30 days. The shipped Background Check Expiring notification can email the care team 30 days before (see Notifications in the Communications manual).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ZxcfoJQWCl", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example
The children's ministry requires a criminal background check and child safety training for nursery workers. When Anna volunteers, the office orders her check and records it as Requested. Two weeks later the provider clears her, and the office sets Cleared with the date. Anna can now be scheduled in the nursery. Three years later, her check shows on Checks Expiring a month before it ends.", "col": 12}}]
